root_cause.text: In smb2_unlink(), the iov arrays (open_iov and close_iov) are not zero-initialized before being assigned to rqst structures, so if SMB2_open_init() or SMB2_close_init() fails, the error cleanup functions (SMB2_open_free, SMB2_close_free, smb2_set_related) operate on uninitialized memory leading to a kernel oops.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "If SMB2_open_init() or SMB2_close_init() fails (e.g. reconnect), the iovs set @rqst will be left uninitialised, hence calling SMB2_open_free(), SMB2_close_free() or smb2_set_related() on them will oops." The patch adds `memset(open_iov, 0, sizeof(open_iov));` and `memset(&close_iov, 0, sizeof(close_iov));` before setting them in `rqst`, and moves `smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]);` after the error check to avoid calling it on failure.

intent_record.how: Ensures the open_iov array is zero-initialized, preventing use of stale stack data in the SMB2 request.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential uninitialized memory and ensure compound close request is marked related only after successful initialization.
intent_record.what: Added memset to zero-initialize close_iov before use, and moved smb2_set_related(&rqst[1]) after the error check for SMB2_close_init.
intent_record.how: Ensures close_iov is properly zeroed, and smb2_set_related is only called when SMB2_close_init succeeds, preventing marking a failed request as part of a compound.
